title: What a sponge city can do: Basel
purpose: One column per action. Row 1: what is possible, for whom. Row 2: what Basel is already doing (verified, or visibly empty). Row 3: where the potential is, with numbers from open data. Row 4: what data is missing, who holds it and the hack that fills or works around the gap. Band: how to get there (our proposals).

city_findings.text: Of about 1,650 ha of sealed ground in Basel-Stadt, 296 ha (18 %) lies on Allmend parcels and 1,353 ha (82 %) on other parcels: 601 ha buildings, 490 ha other paving (courtyards, forecourts, yards, parking, rail and industrial areas) and 262 ha of road surface.
city_findings.method: Each land-cover polygon is assigned to the parcel containing its representative point; Allmend = parcel type 'Allmendparzelle'.
limitations: Polygons crossing parcel boundaries count wholly to one parcel
'Other parcels' include land owned by the canton, municipalities and SBB, not only private owners
Parcel data carries no owner field

city_findings.text: The canton states: "The greatest potential lies in the many large and small private open spaces of our city."
137.7 km of streets rated sponge-suitable by traffic lie in heat areas marked Fokus (77.9 km) or Verbessern (59.8 km).
city_findings.method: Middle vertex of each segment's longest part, tested against the heat focus polygons; lengths from the canton's segment table.
limitations: Traffic is the only suitability criterion; utilities, groundwater and space are not in the rating
One point per segment decides its heat area

city_findings.text: 231 of 334 active or upcoming permitted works (snapshot 3 October 2026) lie within 60 m of those suitable streets in heat areas.
city_findings.method: Permit point within 60 m of the middle vertex of a suitable segment in a Fokus or Verbessern area; upcoming = permit ends October 2026 or later.
limitations: Permits are not a coordinated works plan
60 m is a screening radius, not a design rule

levers.name: Rules
levers.text: Ask for sponge-city requirements (water paths, root space, unsealed share) in every building plan, as Klybeck's plan is being drafted.

levers.name: Dig once by default
levers.text: Check every street permit near a suitable street in a heat area for a sponge rebuild; publish a coordinated multi-year works plan.

levers.name: Money
levers.text: Prioritise the 2026 private greening fund for courtyards in heat areas; state explicitly that disconnected roofs pay a lower rainwater fee.

levers.name: Standards
levers.text: Set a root-space target for every new street tree (Bern uses 36 m³) and a standard for kerb inlets into green.

levers.name: Data
levers.text: Publish gully points and drainage type per street, tree-pit sizes, a green-roof inventory and parking geometry (the Data Charter asks).

levers.name: People
levers.text: Invite residents to water young trees and report blocked gullies; advise owners of large courtyards directly.

access_states.open: Directly available and reusable from an official or public source
access_states.registered: Available through a login or bounded self-service request
access_states.restricted: Exists, but released only for a legitimate area, project or purpose
access_states.operator-held: The infrastructure operator holds the authoritative detail
access_states.project-held: Held within a private project, property or professional workflow
access_states.site-check: A decision-quality value must be inspected, sampled, surveyed or tested locally
access_states.unknown: We do not yet know whether usable evidence exists or who holds it

access_note: Access states follow wrapper/data-charter-map/docs/GATEKEEPERS.md. 'sourced' means an official page states the access rule; 'assumed' is our expectation.

leitungskataster.name: Leitungskataster (Grundbuch- und Vermessungsamt)
leitungskataster.role: Overview of all supply and disposal lines in public space; released case by case as B-Daten, e.g. for planning and building projects; no depths.

operators.name: Network operators (Werke)
operators.role: Only the operators give depths; they must be contacted before digging.

tba-aue.name: Tiefbauamt and Amt für Umwelt und Energie
tba-aue.role: Review the drainage plan (GEP), the basis for property-drainage permits and municipal rainwater management.

stadtgaertnerei.name: Stadtgärtnerei
stadtgaertnerei.role: Maintains the city's trees and the tree cadastre.

owner.name: Property owner and their engineer
owner.role: Hold building, roof and house-drainage records.

field.name: Qualified field team
field.role: Survey, coring, infiltration test, arborist review.

public.name: Residents and team
public.role: Visible, time-stamped observations; never asset records.

hack_kinds.derive: Compute from open inputs; result is derived and named with its method
hack_kinds.digitise: Trace a published map or document into data; keeps its date and scale
hack_kinds.annotate: People mark visible features on open imagery or own photos; candidates, reviewed
hack_kinds.observe: Structured site observation (Rain Walk); time-stamped, reviewable
hack_kinds.request: Ask the gatekeeper with a bounded, polygon-specific question
hack_kinds.site-test: Commission the measurement that only exists on site
hack_kinds.design-around: Choose an intervention that does not depend on the missing fact

prototypes.constraint-simulator: Toggle a gatekeeper's answer; see the intervention family change
prototypes.annotation: Manual marking of visible features on the orthophoto or photos
prototypes.rain-walk: Five-minute on-site checklist, kept on the phone
prototypes.overlay: Open or digitised layer added to the map or street profile
